# Jubilees Chapter 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abram's Rejection of Idols; Abram's Prayer; The Divine Call; Journey to Canaan

---

**12:1** It came to pass in the sixth week, in the seventh year thereof, that Abram said to Terah his father: "Father!"

**12:2** He answered: "Here I am, my son." Abram said: "What help or profit do we get from these idols that you worship and bow down before?"

**12:3** "There is no spirit in them — they are mute forms and a delusion of the heart. Do not worship them."

**12:4** "Worship the God of heaven, who causes the rain and the dew to fall upon the earth and does everything upon the earth, who created all things by his word, and all life is from before his face."

**12:5** "Why do you worship things that have no spirit in them? They are the work of human hands. You carry them on your shoulders, and you receive no profit from them. They are a great shame to those who make them and a delusion of the heart to those who worship them."

**12:6** "Do not worship them."

**12:7** His father answered: "I know this too, my son — but what am I to do with a people who have made me serve before them?"

**12:8** "If I tell them the truth, they will kill me, for their hearts cling to them in worship and honor."

**12:9** "Keep silent, my son, lest they kill you."

**12:10** Abram spoke these things also to Nahor his brother, but Nahor was angry with him and would not listen, for his heart was attached to the idols.

**12:11** Abram arose in the night and burned the house of the idols; he burned everything that was in the house. No one knew.

**12:12** They arose in the night and tried to save their gods from the fire.

**12:13** Haran rushed to save them, but the fire blazed over him; he was burned in the fire and died in Ur of the Chaldees before his father Terah, and they buried him.

**12:14** Terah went out from Ur of the Chaldees — he and his sons — to go to the land of Lebanon and the land of Canaan. He settled in the land of Haran, and Abram lived with his father in Haran for two weeks of years.

**12:15** In the forty-first jubilee, in the third year of the first week, Abram returned to his father's house. Of Terah's sons, Nahor remained there, and Haran was dead.

**12:16** In the sixth year of the second week of the forty-first jubilee, Abram sat up at night and observed the stars from evening until morning to determine what the coming year's rains would be like. He sat alone as he observed.

**12:17** A thought came into his heart, and he said: "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and the sun — all are in the hand of the LORD. Why am I searching them out?"

**12:18** "If he desires, he causes rain to fall, morning and evening; if he desires, he withholds it. All things are in his hand."

**12:19** He prayed that night, saying: "My God, God Most High, you alone are my God. You and your dominion I have chosen. You created all things; all things are the work of your hands."

**12:20** "Deliver me from the hands of evil spirits who have dominion over the thoughts of men's hearts, and do not let them lead me astray from you, my God."

**12:21** "Establish me and my descendants forever, so that we do not go astray from this time forward and forever."

**12:22** He said: "Should I return to Ur of the Chaldees, where people seek my face to bring me back? Or should I remain here in this place?"

**12:23** "The right path lies before you. Prosper it in the hands of your servant, that he may fulfill it, and may I not walk in the error of my heart, O my God."

**12:24** He finished speaking and praying, and then a word of the LORD was sent to him through me, saying: "Get up and go from your country and from your kindred and from your father's house to a land which I will show you. I will make you a great nation, I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be blessed in the earth; and in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed."

**12:25** "And I will care for all your descendants under the sun; your descendants shall be like the sand of the seashore, and I will give your descendants a great land to inherit forever."

**12:26** He arose and took Sarai his wife and Lot the son of Haran his brother, and went to the land of Canaan. He came into the land of Asshur, proceeded to Shechem, and dwelt near a great oak.

**12:27** He saw that the land was very pleasant — from the entrance of Hamath to the great oak.

**12:28** The LORD said to him: "To you and to your descendants I will give this land."

**12:29** He built an altar there and offered a burnt offering to the LORD, who had appeared to him.

**12:30** He moved from there to the mountain between Bethel on the west and Ai on the east, and pitched his tent there.

**12:31** He saw that the land was wide and good, and everything grew on it: vines and figs and pomegranates, oaks and ilex, terebinths and olive trees, cedars and cypresses and date palms and all manner of trees, and there was water in the mountains.

**12:32** He blessed the LORD who had brought him out from Ur of the Chaldees and had safely conducted him to this land.

---
*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows LOGOS throughout. "Through me" (v.24) preserved as the angel of the presence explicitly identifies itself — a structural feature of Jubilees. "God Most High" (v.19) = El Elyon retained as divine title. The botanical catalog (v.31) preserved in full as Jubilees' description of the Promised Land's fertility.*
